stories.title: Protests erupt in Tunisia after migrant boat sinks
stories.summary: The Tunisian city of Ben Guerdane erupted in protest on Saturday night one day after a boat carrying 15 migrants sank off the country's southeastern coast. Protesters blocked roads and set fire to tyres after the news of the shipwreck was announced.

stories.title: From cardboard to cosplay: Kenya’s anime fans turn creativity into culture
stories.summary: Thousands of anime and manga fans gathered in Nairobi for one of Africa’s biggest cosplay conventions, transforming recycled materials, craft skills and imagination into elaborate costumes. For many enthusiasts, the event is more than entertainment—it is a space for creativity, friendship and self-expression. More than 4,000 people attended the latest Otamatsuri anime and manga convention in Nairobi, according to organiser Jotham Micah. The event brought together fans dressed as characters from popular Japanese franchises including. One Piece, Naruto and Gachiakuta, highlighting the growing popularity of Japanese pop culture in Kenya. Micah, co-founder of entertainment company Movie Jabber, said anime and manga have increasingly crossed cultural boundaries. "I think the different sectors or cultural aspects of entertainment, the subcultures are key," he said. "It gives people life, it gives people inspiration, and it's fun and entertaining." For many Kenyan cosplayers, creating elaborate costumes means finding affordable and unconventional materials. Julius Mokaya, a 34-year-old building caretaker and two-time winner of the convention's costume competition, cannot afford to import expensive costumes. Instead, he uses cardboard and other materials collected from recycling bins. His small apartment is filled with homemade weapons, masks and accessories.

stories.title: Putin signs decree on measures to protect critical infrastructure
stories.summary: According to the decree, the Russian government may assume temporary control over critical infrastructure sites, when owners neglect security protocols or delay necessary repairs
article_sentences: Russian authorities will now have the power to impose temporary management on critical infrastructure facilities, if their owners fail to implement or restore security measures in a timely manner.
This provision is established under a new decree signed by President Vladimir Putin.

According to the decree, the Russian government may assume temporary control over critical infrastructure sites, including the fuel and energy sector, industrial enterprises, communication networks, utilities, transport and logistics infrastructure, and energy facilities such as nuclear power plants - when owners neglect security protocols or delay necessary repairs.
The measure also applies to life support systems, potentially hazardous facilities, and other sites vital to the nation's security, economic stability, and public well-being.

The decision to implement these measures stems from the increasing security threats faced by Russia's critical infrastructure amid ongoing operations, and aligns with the laws on Martial Law, Defense, and Security.
The decree takes effect immediately upon its official publication.

stories.title: Guinea: Conakry residents grapple with aftermath of landfill disaster
stories.summary: Residents in Guinea's capital Conakry have been left reeling after part of a landfill fell on to neighbouring homes following heavy rains. The incident has claimed 30 lives.
